evidence.text: Security Council meeting S/PV.9771, 31 October 2024. The United States draft S/2024/796 was adopted as resolution 2756 (2024), with 12 votes in favour, zero against, two abstentions (Mozambique and the Russian Federation), and one member not participating (Algeria).

Algeria proposed S/2024/797, which would note nine consecutive years without an OHCHR visit, and S/2024/798, which would have the Council consider expanding MINURSO's mandate to monitor, help investigate, report on and follow up on humanitarian-law and human-rights violations. They received 6–0–9 and 5–0–10 respectively and neither secured enough votes to be adopted.

Resolution 2756 extended the MINURSO mandate until 31 October 2025 and urged increased cooperation with OHCHR, including facilitating visits. The proposed language to consider adding monitoring functions was not incorporated.

Speaking for Algeria, Bendjama introduced two amendments concerning human rights. He cited the report documenting the ninth consecutive year without an OHCHR visit and argued that MINURSO should have a human-rights monitoring component, as other missions do.

After voting, Bendjama explained Algeria's deliberate non-participation on the final resolution and said the penholder had disregarded Algeria's views. He reaffirmed that the Sahrawi people should be free to choose their future.

After declaring that she was now speaking as Switzerland's representative, Baeriswyl said Switzerland backed S/2024/797 because OHCHR had been unable to visit for nine consecutive years. She said Switzerland abstained on S/2024/798 to ensure continuity of MINURSO's work after consensus eluded the negotiations.

In that national statement, Baeriswyl said Switzerland supported the final resolution, favoured human-rights protection and stressed support for the Personal Envoy and the Special Representative. After the statement she resumed her functions as Council President.

Gives the 31 October 2025 extension, the call to facilitate OHCHR visits and the absence of an adopted MINURSO monitoring expansion. Distinguishes Council acts from national statements.

packet.answer: On 31 October 2024, draft S/2024/796 became resolution 2756 (2024) by 12–0–2. Algeria did not participate [MAIN]. Algeria’s S/2024/797 on nine years without an OHCHR visit failed 6–0–9. S/2024/798, to consider expanding MINURSO for rights monitoring, failed 5–0–10 [AMEND]. Algeria favoured MINURSO monitoring and said the penholder disregarded its views, explaining its decision not to participate [DZ-A; DZ-B]. Speaking nationally, Baeriswyl said Switzerland supported S/2024/797 and abstained on S/2024/798 to protect continuity of the mission [CH-A]. The Council extended MINURSO until 31 October 2025 and urged cooperation including OHCHR visits. It did not add the monitoring functions [TEXT].
